studies.label: Lab experiment: Product Improvement Task with vs. without ChatGPT
studies.cluster_se_treatment: No session clustering is reported. Students were individually randomized before the experiment, but the two conditions ran in separate sessions. The t-tests and ANCOVAs treat participants as independent (PDF pp. 10 and 16).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Participants and Table 1 headers; analyzed arm counts only
counts_source.quote: The control group for the present study contained 68 university students and the experimental group contained 77 participants

arms.name: Experimental (ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the Product Improvement Task with ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus) open in a second browser tab, following a short description with example prompts and responses. Task instructions explicitly referred to ChatGPT assistance. Participants also answered additional self-efficacy questions (PDF pp. 10, 13).

arms.name: Control (no ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the same Product Improvement Task in a single browser tab without ChatGPT. Both conditions could access additional browser tools, but no participant did so (PDF p. 10).

studies.task: Generate three original and useful improvements to an ordinary stuffed bunny to help Mattel achieve higher sales than the Lego Group (PDF pp. 12-13).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Experimental Procedure; model/product release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: Open Science Framework, https://osf.io/q6wtu (PDF p. 9); hypotheses on PDF pp. 8-9. The manuscript states that the experimental design and hypotheses were preregistered. The registration itself was not used as a source for this reconciliation.

studies.shared_sample: Per forms/c123.json, sample_overlap: Urban et al. Its preprint states the overlap on p. 9. This overlap is supplied by the reconciled form; the c123 manuscript does not identify the later paper.

open_items: The source prints arm sizes but no combined analyzed total. Study n_analyzed and estimate n_total are null rather than computed by summing the arms. The reconciled screening form gives a combined total, but it is not printed in this manuscript.

The paper states individual random assignment before the experiment and no exclusions, but does not print counts at assignment, the randomization mechanism, or the number of assigned volunteers who did not attend. Randomized counts remain null.

PIT score construction is incomplete: the paper does not identify the PIT raters or explain how their ratings and the three solutions become one participant score. The inferential analyses support participant-level coding, but the aggregation procedure remains unspecified.
The arms ran in separate sessions with at most five people per session. Session counts and scheduling are unreported; no adjustment for session clustering is described.

The manuscript names no primary outcome or ranking among the preregistered H1 dimensions (PDF pp. 8-9). The OSF registration was not used as a source for this reconciliation; preregistered_primary remains not_stated.
No model release year is printed. The tool name is retained verbatim from the Methods, and ai_tool.year is null.
The manuscript does not specify the standardizer for its reported d values. The unadjusted records retain the printed participant-level arm SDs.
Adjusted ANCOVA arm means, differences, SEs, coefficients, and confidence limits are not printed. The group-by-task analysis likewise lacks change summaries and a complete model specification.
Figure 1 presents z-score means and confidence bars without numerical labels. No values were digitized or inferred from the graph.
The journal version of record is not the PDF on file; the extraction is limited to the accepted manuscript and its included appendix.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10 against the saved accepted manuscript. The entire markdown conversion was read in chunks through Appendix 1. All cited PDF pages were text-extracted with PyMuPDF, and Figure 1 was inspected directly from its embedded image without saving another file. PDF and printed page numbers agree. The comparison file flags only clusters_per_arm and contains no unmatched estimates; the explanatory cluster_se_treatment wording difference is also resolved explicitly. All seven numerical specifications agree between A and B and were independently confirmed in the PDF. A's slugs are retained; B's different slugs and remaining narrative wording identify the same results. No estimates were added or removed. All three screening-form outcomes and their full-sample contrasts are covered; excluded baseline, self-report, and nonrandomized associations are listed in not_extracted. The shared counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person fields were rechecked against the procedure, participant table, rating definitions, rubric, and results. Quality maps to usefulness, elaboration to elaboration, and originality to novelty (PDF p. 13 and Appendix 1). The paper does not print a combined analyzed total, so the screening form's combined count is not copied or reconstructed. All statistics are transcribed without calculating totals, effects, SEs, or intervals; quotes preserve printed precision. The unadjusted, ANCOVA, and group-by-task records share participants and must not be treated as independent studies. For a specification tie under codebook section 8, the manuscript identifies ANCOVA as its main hypothesis-testing analysis (PDF p. 16); originality is preferred under the construct hierarchy, while preregistered primary status remains unconfirmed. Country is inferred from the laboratory being at the first author's institution (PDF p. 9) and its Prague, Czech Republic address (PDF p. 1), consistent with the reconciled form. Sample overlap with c594 is carried from the form and was not independently reverified against that later paper. No across_people or after_ai outcome is reported.

resolutions.decision: Use null. People were individually randomized before the experiment. Separate sessions do not establish cluster assignment, and the manuscript prints no number of sessions or randomized clusters per arm. No cluster count is inferred.
resolutions.quote: Male and female students who volunteered for the experiment were randomly assigned to either the control condition (task resolution without ChatGPT) or the experimental one (task resolution with ChatGPT) prior to the experiment.

resolutions.b: No session clustering is reported. Students were individually randomized before the experiment, but the two conditions ran in separate sessions. The t-tests and ANCOVAs treat participants as independent (PDF pp. 10 and 16).
resolutions.decision: Retain B's explicit description. The paper reports individual assignment and separate sessions, but its independent-samples tests and ANCOVAs describe no session clustering. Participant-level uncertainty is retained; unreported session counts and scheduling remain open items.
resolutions.locator: PDF p. 16, Results, analysis paragraph below Table 2; separate sessions on PDF p. 10

review_corrections.basis: PDF p. 10: 'The experiment was held in a quiet room with a maximum of five participants at one time. The control group and experimental groups had separate sessions.' Every session ran one arm, so under the codebook section 3 session rule (added during Phase 2, 2026-10-10, for review) the session is the assignment unit. The number of sessions is not printed (clusters_per_arm stays null). The t-tests and ANCOVAs treat participants as independent, so these records are not pooled while the rule stands.

Sum of the printed analyzed arm counts (77 + 68), between-person design: 'The control group for the present study contained 68 university students and the experimental group contained 77 participants' (PDF p. 11, Participants); no exclusions (PDF p. 10). The paper prints no total; the counts pass (extraction/checks/c123.counts.json) found none either.
